verdict.line: You lose if you let him free-farm stacks past level 6; you win if you zone his Q (Siphoning Strike) off the wave before then.

brief.thesis: Nasus is a melee farm champion whose entire win condition is landing Siphoning Strike (Q, 255 range) on minions — every stack he misses is gone forever. Urgot's Corrosive Charge (Q, 800 range) and auto range let him poke Nasus off cs without ever entering his Q range, which is exactly why Urgot holds both the lane and solo-kill edge here (52.9% over 1065 games). Let the wave sit and he scales into a problem; deny it and he never recovers.

theirWindow.when: Wither lands and stacks are high
theirWindow.what: Wither ages your Movement and Attack Speed, letting Nasus close the gap and unload stacked autos while burning Spirit Fire under you. Disengage immediately rather than trading autos — don't try to out-DPS a slowed fight.

yourWindow.when: Siphoning Strike and Wither both down
yourWindow.what: Walk up and land Corrosive Charge, then commit Disdain to shield through his melee range and shove him off the wave or into tower range. Before level 6 he has no tool to punish this.

start.why: Most-picked start (87.6%, 54.8% WR over 1196 games) — the extra sustain and auto damage fund the short poke trades you want, not a melee shove war.

boots.why: 49.3% pick, 54.5% WR over 642 games — Nasus's damage is entirely stacked-auto physical, so flat reduction on autos matters more than slow resist here.

core.why: Shred stacks from Q/W/E poke whittle his armor down fast, undercutting the tankiness he buys to survive your range.
Survivability for when Wither connects and he closes the gap to auto you down.
Highest-winrate third item in the data (58% over 176 games) — scales your own tankiness as the fight drags into his late-game power spike.

situational.when: if he's built up Soul Eater lifesteal and is winning extended melee trades
if his healing from stacked Q and lifesteal is stalling your kills
if you need an early grievous wounds rush to stop him sustaining through poke
if he starts split-pushing and you need to catch him across the map

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the ranged auto-poke plan directly — three hits exposes him to bonus damage right as he's forced to step up for cs, turning every farm attempt into a losing trade.

summoners.why: Highest pick rate by far (88.4%, 55% WR) — Ignite denies Soul Eater healing during your level 2-5 all-in windows and secures kills before he can scale out of them.

playing.title: Poke before he farms
playing.detail: Land Corrosive Charge on the wave to deny Siphoning Strike attempts — every missed stack is permanent lost scaling for him.

playing.title: All-in on cooldown windows
playing.detail: When his Q and Wither are both down, commit Disdain to close distance, trample through his melee range, and shove him off the wave.

playing.title: Don't auto-duel into Wither
playing.detail: Once Wither lands, his attack/move speed edge over you kicks in — disengage instead of trading autos while slowed.

playing.title: Respect Spirit Fire zoning
playing.detail: His armor-shred flame swings extended trades his way; don't stand in it to farm or fight.

playing.title: Sequence Q into Purge
playing.detail: Purge prioritizes champions you've already hit with Q or E, so poke first, then follow with Purge to close out short trades for plates.

playing.title: Track his ultimate timer
playing.detail: Fury of the Sands is a 120-second cooldown that transforms him in skirmishes — don't fully commit if he's healthy and it's up.

playing.title: Build through his sustain
playing.detail: Soul Eater lifesteal scales his staying power in long trades — Bramble Vest or Executioner's Calling cuts that off if the lane stalls.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, boots, runes, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are measured from live games on the current patch; the mechanical and timing reasoning behind them is my own read of the matchup.

stats.opponentTip: Do not let Nasus farm lane easily by contesting lane during early game. Gain control over lane and use it to get turret plates or to kill him.
